If a pan of oil catches fire, do not throw water on it.
Water makes the fire bigger, and throws burning oil across your kitchen.
Do not pick up the pan.
And do not grab an ordinary fire extinguisher. It can blast burning oil around the room.
Slide a lid over the pan. No lid? Use a baking sheet.
Then leave it covered until the pan is cool, or the fire can start again.
Fire in the oven? Turn it off, and keep the door shut.
Flames out of the pan? Get out, close the door behind you, and call the fire service.
And next time, stay by the pan. If the oil starts to smoke, turn the burner off.
Cooking left alone starts more of these fires than anything else.
